findings.summary: update_email writes to the DB but does not invalidate the read-through cache, leaving stale user data.
findings.failure_scenario: Call get_user(1) (caches the user with old email), then update_email(1, "new@x.com"), then get_user(1) again. Because self._cache[1] is never invalidated/updated in update_email, get_user returns the cached user object with the old email instead of the updated one.

findings.summary: update_email writes to the DB but fails to invalidate/update the read-through cache, so get_user returns stale email data.
findings.failure_scenario: Call get_user(1) -> caches {"email": "old@x.com"}. Then update_email(1, "new@x.com") writes the new email to the DB but does not touch self._cache. A subsequent get_user(1) finds user_id already in _cache and returns the stale cached record with "old@x.com" instead of the updated email. The fix is to do self._cache.pop(user_id, None) (or update the cached entry) inside update_email.

findings.summary: compute_discount sums every line item into the discount base and ignores the 'type' field, so non-discountable items (e.g. gift cards) wrongly inflate the coupon discount.
findings.failure_scenario: Cart with line_items=[{"price": 5000, "type": "gift_card"}]. Gift cards are conventionally excluded from coupon discounts, but base=5000 yields a discount of 500 cents (capped by DISCOUNT_CAP=2000). The function should filter on item["type"] before summing; instead it discounts items that should be ineligible. The docstring explicitly calling out 'type' signals it must be used.

findings.summary: compute_discount ignores each line item's 'type', so the discount is applied to every item including types that should be excluded (e.g. gift cards / non-discountable items).
findings.failure_scenario: A cart containing line_items=[{"price": 5000, "type": "gift_card"}] yields base=5000 and a 500-cent discount, even though gift cards (the reason 'type' is documented) should not be discountable. The discount is over-applied.

findings.summary: min() with DISCOUNT_CAP does not guard against a negative base, so a cart whose line items net to a negative total produces a negative (i.e., wrong-direction) discount.
findings.failure_scenario: If line_items contains a refund/credit line with a negative price such that base < 0, base*1000//10000 is negative and min(negative, 2000) returns that negative value, so compute_discount returns a negative discount instead of 0.
